posts.note: Satire that maps the Sept 30, 2025 continuing-resolution standoff onto the newsletter 'running out of words'. Shutdown calls logged with the mapping explained; one real-bill aside (S.1717) logged.
Day-two shutdown satire with a photo retrospective. Shutdown calls logged with sincere=true where the underlying federal claim reads as sincere; newsletter-format jokes logged with sincere=false.
Fully fictional Lord of the Rings parody of a shutdown press conference. One character line logged for recall with sincere=false and own_claim=false.
Literacy and health-literacy essay; all claims are past or present analysis. The Radial content work is present tense.
GLP-1s and alcohol essay. Core forecast: population GLP-1 use might drive alcohol use 'off a cliff'. Two quoted third-party industry forecasts (SipSource, IWSR) logged with own_claim=false.
Eulogy for Nolan Williams. Forward-looking claims are a paraphrase of Philip K. Dick applied to Williams's treatments, plus a quoted line on Texas ibogaine trial funding.

Suicide-prevention guide; the advice is normative and was not logged. One borderline 'isn't approved yet' line logged. The line on health plans excluding TMS for suicidal ideation is a 'should' with no prediction and was not logged.
Radical acceptance essay; only the closing Radial expansion line (St. Louis and Chattanooga 'soon') is forward-looking.

statements.quote: Absent compromise, further words are unlikely to be authorized. This will lead to a crisis for the newsletter and a complete shutdown of services, at least among articles that you’d want to read.
statements.context: Satirical post (dated 2025-09-29) that maps the looming US federal government shutdown, with a continuing-resolution deadline on Tuesday Sept 30, 2025, onto the newsletter 'running out of words'. The author says that absent a compromise no further words will be authorized and the newsletter shuts down.
statements.note: Satire of the federal shutdown standoff; literal subject is the newsletter's word supply. Underlying claim (shutdown absent a CR compromise) reads as sincere. Compound: 'unlikely' plus 'will'. Coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: many critical pieces of education and satire are, as of the looming deadline for a continuing resolution on Tuesday, apt to shut down entirely
statements.context: Same satire. The author says the newsletter's education and satire pieces are apt to shut down entirely at the continuing-resolution deadline on Tuesday (Sept 30, 2025); that is, the shutdown starts when the CR deadline passes.
statements.horizon_text: the looming deadline for a continuing resolution on Tuesday
statements.note: Satirical restatement of the first shutdown call with a dated horizon (the Tuesday CR deadline).

statements.quote: Senator Spooner, on Sunday, said there will be “huge pressure” on Readers to agree to talks to restore healthcare articles, which he said threaten to not amuse those working in rural hospitals and dramatically hike insurance premiums.
statements.context: Parody of a real Sunday-show quote by a Senate leader, transposed into the newsletter satire: 'Senator Spooner' predicts huge pressure on the other side to negotiate on healthcare and warns of dramatic insurance premium hikes.
statements.note: Fictionalized third-party quote (parody of a Senate Democratic leader). Not the author's stance; logged for recall.

statements.quote: I’m thrilled to have the support of Funpublicans in both the House and the Senate; however, in this case, it won’t be enough. Sixty votes are required to avert running out of things to say
statements.context: In satirical voice, the author says Republican ('Funpublican') support in the House and Senate will not be enough; sixty Senate votes are required to avert the shutdown. The underlying claim is that the House-passed continuing resolution fails the Senate threshold and the shutdown proceeds.
statements.note: Satirical framing; the underlying claim (CR fails the 60-vote threshold, shutdown proceeds) reads as sincere.

statements.quote: Maybe they even pass the S.1717 - Ensuring Patient Access to Critical Breakthrough Products Act of 2025 as part of the compromise?
statements.context: Closing aside of the shutdown satire. The author speculates that Congress might pass S.1717, the Ensuring Patient Access to Critical Breakthrough Products Act of 2025 (a bill on Medicare coverage of FDA breakthrough-designated products), as part of a shutdown compromise.
entities: S.1717 Ensuring Patient Access to Critical Breakthrough Products Act of 2025
statements.note: Phrased as a question with 'Maybe'; hopeful speculation about a real bill inside a satirical post. The author has an interest in device (TMS) coverage.

statements.quote: a compromise on a Continuing Resolution to supply enough additional words for a “word-based” newsletter seems increasingly unlikely
statements.context: Post dated 2025-09-30, the day before the federal shutdown deadline. The author says a compromise on a Continuing Resolution seems increasingly unlikely, mapping the federal CR standoff onto the newsletter's supply of words.
statements.note: Satire; the underlying claim (no CR compromise, shutdown follows) reads as sincere. Restates the 2025-09-29 call.

statements.quote: Blog posts (pre-written) educating us about “ what is treatment resistant depression ” will run dry soon, I’m sure.
statements.context: Joke plug for pre-written Radial blog posts on treatment-resistant depression, which the author says will run dry soon once the newsletter's 'words' run out.
statements.note: Joke about own-organization content; no sincere underlying claim. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: They need to realize that, without nouns and verbs, this newsletter will cease to be relevant to the American people.
statements.context: Parody quote attributed to 'Funpublican leaders' who press the other side to back a House-passed funding bill; the fictional leaders predict the newsletter will cease to be relevant without funding.
statements.note: Fictionalized third-party quote; parody of shutdown messaging. Not the author's stance; logged for recall.

statements.quote: Today, on the eve of a complete shutdown of this newsletter, we present some pictures and music as a retrospective of what we can show
statements.context: The author asserts the newsletter shutdown happens the next day (Oct 1, 2025), that is, the federal shutdown takes effect when the CR deadline passes; the post offers photos and music as a preview of a wordless newsletter.
statements.note: Satire; the underlying claim (shutdown begins Oct 1, 2025) reads as sincere and is stated as near-certain by 'on the eve of'.

statements.quote: As threatened, the publication might end up being a series of pictures.
statements.context: The author says the newsletter might become picture-only if the 'word' shutdown proceeds.
statements.note: Joke about the newsletter's format; no sincere underlying claim. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: We may need to move to airline-style cartoons or other figurative renderings to make it all make sense.
statements.context: Closing joke: absent a compromise, the newsletter may have to use airline-safety-card style cartoons instead of words. Preceded by the wish 'Let's hope there is some compromise that breaks the word-block'.
statements.note: Joke; no sincere underlying claim. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Their shutdown will leave each ringbearer unpowered, including all 7 dwarf lords, nine elderly men, now doomed to die, and even hobble the three elf-lords, putting vital mithril-delving and even tree-care programs for Ents at risk, and jeopardizing flood insurance for millions of Isengardians during the fallout from the rainy season in and around Helm’s Deep’s failing dam.
statements.context: Fully fictional Lord of the Rings parody of a shutdown press conference, dated 2025-10-01. The character 'Sauron' lists the harms the shutdown 'will' cause; it parodies real shutdown-day political messaging about lapsed programs.
statements.note: Fictional character speech; no sincere underlying forecast. Logged for recall only.

statements.quote: So I hope you can all now join me as we celebrate the fall of alcohol, which I am depositing is in part due to the rise of GLP-1s.
statements.context: Thesis of the post (dated 2025-10-06): alcohol consumption is falling ('the fall of alcohol') and the author attributes part of the decline to rising GLP-1 use (semaglutide, tirzepatide). A present-trend causal claim that sets up the later forecast that GLP-1s might drive alcohol use 'off a cliff'.
statements.note: Present-tense trend claim with an implied continuation; logged as borderline. 'depositing' is a transcription of 'positing'.

statements.quote: Based on a June 2025 news release, SipSource forecasts that after “growing decline levels seen between 2022 and 2024,” sales of rum, U.S. whiskey, vodka, and brandy/cognac “ are expected to largely flatten by the first half of 2026, albeit in negative territory.”
statements.context: Third-party industry forecast (SipSource, June 2025) quoted as evidence that drinking is coming down after the pandemic spike: spirits sales (rum, US whiskey, vodka, brandy/cognac) are expected to flatten by the first half of 2026 while still in decline.
statements.note: Quoted third-party forecast used as supporting evidence; the author does not explicitly adopt it.

statements.quote: IWSR expects strong growth to continue in the years ahead, forecasting a volume CAGR gain of +17% for no-alcohol between 2022 and 2027.
statements.context: Third-party forecast (IWSR) quoted in the section on mocktails and no/low-alcohol drinks booming; the author adds that he is 'excited to hear' it as a consumer and friend of a mocktail company founder.
statements.note: Quoted third-party forecast; the author endorses the direction ('excited to hear') but does not adopt the number.

statements.quote: It might be enough to drive alcohol use off a cliff!
statements.context: After citing a 24-person semaglutide RCT and noting that 12% of US adults report GLP-1 use, the author says open-label, often higher-dose GLP-1 use at population scale might be enough to drive alcohol use off a cliff (a steep fall in drinking).
statements.note: Core forecast of the post; no quantity or date. Area could also be 'other' (population drinking behavior).

statements.quote: Because it means men are less likely to drink as much, and that means they're less likely to rape women and assault women physically.
statements.context: Section 'Ending Rape Culture By Ending Drinking Culture, with GLP-1s'. The author argues that GLP-1 uptake means men drink less and therefore commit fewer sexual and physical assaults: a causal chain from GLP-1 adoption to less violence against women.
statements.note: Compound causal claim (less drinking leads to less assault); no quantity or date.

statements.quote: I'm gonna miss the CDC when these kinds of numbers are deemed inconvenient by the men in power who find their sexual assaulting impinged upon by such data
statements.context: Parenthetical aside while citing CDC intimate-partner-violence statistics: the author expects CDC data of this kind to become unavailable when 'the men in power' deem it inconvenient, that is, he expects the CDC or its data to be curtailed.
statements.note: Sardonic political aside that implies expected suppression of CDC data. Borderline.

statements.quote: Complaining about it doesn't do any good, but encouraging men everywhere to pursue GLP-1 treatment just might.
statements.context: Closing line: after saying he is excited for a world without alcohol-driven sexual assault risk, the author says encouraging men to take GLP-1s 'just might' reduce that risk.
statements.note: Hedged restatement of the causal claim that GLP-1 uptake reduces assault.

statements.quote: As for Nolan's role in the future of care for human suffering, I can only say that his work and ideas will evolve into a stunning set of treatments.
statements.context: Eulogy (dated 2025-10-11) for Nolan Williams of Stanford, developer of SAINT / Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy (accelerated fMRI-guided TMS) and ibogaine researcher, who founded companies to bring the work to market. The author paraphrases Philip K. Dick's letter about Blade Runner and applies it to Williams: his work and ideas will evolve into a stunning set of treatments.
statements.note: Explicit paraphrase of a Philip K. Dick quote, adopted as the author's own tribute; eulogistic hyperbole stated as expectation.

statements.quote: The future Nolan saw will be one hell of a commercial success; it will prove invincible and become the standard of care for people suffering in the future.
statements.context: Same paraphrased passage: the author says the treatments Williams envisioned (accelerated fMRI-guided TMS such as SAINT/SNT, ibogaine therapy) will be a major commercial success and will become the standard of care.
statements.note: Compound: commercial success plus standard of care. Paraphrase of Philip K. Dick's Blade Runner letter. The author offers SAINT-type care at Radial.

statements.quote: In an unprecedented move, Texas is poised to launch a public-private partnership to fund FDA-approvable drug development trials of ibogaine, backed by $50M in state matching funds
statements.context: Block-quoted text presented as background on Williams's ibogaine advocacy with elected leaders: Texas is poised to launch a public-private partnership, backed by $50M in state matching funds, to fund FDA-approvable ibogaine drug development trials.
statements.note: Appears to be quoted third-party text (news excerpt) introduced with a colon; the author presents it as fact. Coder may treat it as adopted.

statements.quote: This data is limited of course, because some of it isn't approved yet, and other forms of it are not paid for reliably enough to test the hypothesis.
statements.context: After listing ketamine, TMS, SAINT-TMS, psychedelic medicines and magnesium-ibogaine as treatments that can give rapid remission of depression and concurrent suicidality, the author notes that some are not approved 'yet' (which implies expected approval) and others are not reliably paid for.
statements.note: Present-state sentence; the only forward element is the implicit 'yet'. Borderline, logged for recall.

statements.quote: Psychiatric care is available at Radial , in NYC, Myrtle Beach, SC, Conway, SC, La Jolla, CA, and soon St. Louis, MO, and Chattanooga, TN.
statements.context: Closing promotional line (post dated 2025-10-15): the author's company Radial offers care in NYC, Myrtle Beach SC, Conway SC and La Jolla CA, and will soon open in St. Louis MO and Chattanooga TN.
statements.note: Own-organization expansion announcement; coder marks CONTROL. The space before the comma after 'Radial' is in the source text.
